body: For more than three decades, Fairtrade has been making an impact on the way trade works.
Learn about our collective progress alongside farmers, workers, businesses, and partners worldwide in advancing fairer trade.
+37,000 products sold with the Fairtrade MARK in more than 140 countries
Sustainable consumption and production has become the expectation rather than the exception. Fairtrade offers solutions for companies and producers to put fairness at the heart of their operations.

15.10.26 Fairtrade news From Casual Worker to Supervisor: Jacqueline Chepsergon’s 25-year journey in Kenya’s flower Industry Today is the International Day of Rural Women, and it’s a moment to celebrate the critical role and contributions of women in agriculture. This year, Fairtrade is shining a light on Jacqueline Chepsergon, a supervisor at certified flower farm Maji Mazuri Flowers in Kenya. Read more

Today is the International Day of Rural Women, and it’s a moment to celebrate the critical role and contributions of women in agriculture. This year, Fairtrade is shining a light on Jacqueline Chepsergon, a supervisor at certified flower farm Maji Mazuri Flowers in Kenya.

05.10.26 Press releases Fairtrade raises Minimum Price for bananas amid soaring costs for farmers Fairtrade International has increased its Minimum Prices for bananas in direct response to a combination of external pressures negatively impacting producers, including geopolitical instability, climate change, and rising input and logistics costs. Read more

Fairtrade International has increased its Minimum Prices for bananas in direct response to a combination of external pressures negatively impacting producers, including geopolitical instability, climate change, and rising input and logistics costs.

01.10.26 Fairtrade news “Coffee is like raising a child," how Mrs. Rizkani nurtures her crops and her community For Mrs. Rizkani tending a coffee farm is like raising a child, it requires love, patience, and an unwavering commitment to watch something grow. Read more

Achieving meaningful change requires significant systemic shifts. We track our progress through various metrics, so our approach is well-informed and can continuously be improved.
Affoué Angèle Kouassi has farmed cocoa on her own land for 14 years. She participated in Fairtrade’s Women’s School of Leadership in 2021.
